page.h1: HTS Chapter 72: Iron and Steel — Export Markets & Foreign Tariffs on U.S. Goods

seo.title: Tariffs on U.S. Steel & Scrap by Market (HTS Ch. 72) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: What Mexico, Canada, Türkiye, the EU, Thailand, India, Bangladesh and Taiwan charge on U.S. steel and ferrous scrap, by product, with each market's quota, safeguard and scrap-import rules.

intro: Tariffs on U.S. iron and steel split three ways. **Scrap**, a third of the chapter, enters every large scrap market duty-free — Türkiye, Thailand, India, Bangladesh and Taiwan all charge 0% on 7204 — so what decides access is the buyer's import licence, inspection and radiation rules (see each market's regulator). **Finished steel** to Mexico enters free under USMCA, but only if it meets the rule of origin: Mexico's general rate is now 35%. And three markets have put new duties on U.S. finished steel since January 2025: **Canada** a 50% surtax on 7206–7229, the **EU** a 50% duty once its steel quotas are used up, and **India** an 11.5% safeguard duty on flat steel.
valueBasis: FOB value of U.S. exports, as reported by the United States to UN Comtrade.

Scrap, pig iron, ferroalloys and DRI are not on the list, and stainless flat steel and electrical steel can have the surtax remitted.

assumptions: Rates are what U.S.-origin goods pay in November 2026. MFN rates are the World Bank/UNCTAD WITS (TRAINS) simple-average applied rates for one representative six-digit subheading per heading — the subheading with the largest 2025 U.S. exports in that heading (for example 7204.49 for scrap, 7208.51 for hot-rolled plate and 7210.49 for galvanized sheet) — for 2023, the latest year WITS holds, updated where a national 2026 schedule or decree was checked (Mexico, the EU, Bangladesh, Taiwan). National 8–10-digit lines can differ.

Mexico and Canada show the USMCA rate for qualifying goods. Mexico's normal-rate column shows the general rate set by the decree of December 29, 2025 (35% on most Chapter 72 lines from January 1, 2026). USMCA's Chapter 72 rule (HTSUS General Note 11) requires a change of heading group: steel rolled from an imported slab qualifies, steel cold-rolled from imported hot-rolled coil does not.

Canada's cells add the 50% surtax of the United States Surtax Order (Steel and Aluminum 2025) for the 134 tariff items it lists in 7206–7229, and note the lines whose surtax Schedule 6 of the United States Surtax Remission Order (2025) remits. Cold-formed angles, shapes and sections (7216.91) are not on that list; they pay the global 25% Steel Derivative Goods Surtax Order (SOR/2025-267), which does not stack with the U.S. surtax. Other remission (named products and importers, steel for motor-vehicle and aircraft manufacturing) is on Export rules.

The EU cells show the 0% duty and, for products in Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2026/1384, the 50% duty that applies once the quota U.S. steel shares with other countries is used up. Whether a quota is still open on the shipment date is not shown.

India's flat-steel cells add the safeguard duty in force for the year from April 21, 2026 (11.5%); it does not apply above the CIF price floors in the DGTR final findings. India's 0% on scrap is an applied exemption from the statutory rate.
Bangladesh's cells add customs, regulatory and supplementary duty, which Bangladesh collects at the border; VAT and advance taxes are the buyer's business and are left out.

China (not one of the eight markets) charges its MFN rate plus the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods, and many Chapter 72 lines are also on its 2018–2019 counter-tariff lists unless the importer holds an exclusion (see Tariff updates).
